name: Morepen Laboratories Ltd
tagline: A checkered-governance pharma turnaround story now betting its next leg on a surprise CDMO pivot
business_overview: Morepen manufactures pharma APIs and finished formulations (it claims a large share of the US Loratadine/Montelukast generics market) and sells consumer health devices (BP monitors, glucometers) under the Dr. Morepen brand. In 2026 it began pivoting toward CDMO/contract manufacturing after landing a large pharma order.
fundamentals_table: Net profit +422% YoY to Rs 56.4 Cr; revenue +34.1% YoY to Rs 570.1 Cr
fundamentals_narrative: Classic inflection case: the 5-year trailing average (8.73% revenue CAGR, negative trailing ROE) is weak, but the most recent quarter shows a sharp jump (revenue +34%, PAT +422% YoY), driven by early execution on an 823 Cr CDMO order announced roughly 6 months ago. Rs 58 Cr of that order was delivered in Q1 itself, alongside a clean USFDA inspection.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass — stock is near a 52-week high (~Rs 66) after the CDMO news broke.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 64 posts (2015-2026), single batch. Sentiment through 2015-2022 centers on a long-running debt-reduction/turnaround narrative repeatedly overshadowed by governance history (a 2019 SEBI trading ban tied to a 2003 GDR case, a CBI case against promoter Sushil Suri, and a 2025 medical-devices hive-off criticized by some as unfavorable to minority shareholders). The last ~6 posts (Aug 2026) pivot sharply to the new CDMO story.
community_signal: Trusted user Niraj_Punjkaran broke the CDMO story (2026-08-16): '823 cr CDMO order...clean USFDA inspection...swift execution by 58cr delivery by Q1 itself,' but flagged it as unconfirmed — 'lets see it unfold over the next few qtrs.' Trusted user vikasbargale questioned whether it's genuinely CDMO (with development work) or just contract manufacturing (CMO); Niraj_Punjkaran agreed it's presently a CMO relationship pending proof of a pipeline of repeat orders.

trusted_signals.note: Flagged the 823 Cr CDMO/CMO order and clean USFDA inspection as a potential re-rating catalyst, explicitly caveated as unconfirmed pending follow-up orders.
Questioned whether the new business is genuinely CDMO (with development IP) or just contract manufacturing (CMO) — a material distinction for the re-rating thesis.

bse_notes: 2019: Sebi banned Morepen and promoter Sushil Suri from markets over a 2003 GDR-related capital-raising case (historical, resolved/settled, not an active current action). No current active SEBI/BSE action identified this pass.
bull_case: Recent-quarter inflection is real and specific: Rs 823 Cr CDMO/CMO order, Rs 58 Cr already delivered in Q1, clean USFDA inspection — not just narrative
Existing base business (API + consumer diagnostics) already growing (Q1 revenue +34% YoY, PAT +422% YoY) independent of the CDMO story
Trading at a depressed multiple partly attributable to legacy governance overhang, which could re-rate if the CDMO relationship proves durable
bear_case: Trailing 5-year fundamentals are genuinely weak (8.73% revenue CAGR, negative trailing ROE) — the CDMO catalyst is unconfirmed, single-customer, and only one quarter old

Governance history is a real, repeated pattern: 2019 SEBI ban, CBI case against the promoter, past debt restructuring, and a 2025 medical-devices hive-off several posters felt shortchanged minority shareholders
Community itself disputes whether this is true CDMO (sticky, IP-driven, higher-margin) or plain-vanilla CMO (commoditized, competitive) — the bull case hinges on which it turns out to be
Negative operating cash flow flagged by multiple posters in 2023-2025 tied to rising receivables even as sales growth was inconsistent
verdict_headline: A real but single-quarter, single-customer inflection riding on top of a genuinely weak trailing base and a checkered governance history
verdict_reasoning: Per the project's inflection rule, a weak trailing average with a strong, specific, recent-quarter catalyst (the CDMO order, USFDA clearance, and already-delivered revenue) merits a 10x-in-2-3-years tag at low conviction with an explicit unconfirmed caveat, not a flat 'neither'

The community itself — including a trusted user — is withholding full conviction pending confirmation of repeat orders and clarity on CDMO vs CMO economics, which argues for Low rather than Medium conviction
Governance history (SEBI ban, CBI case, minority-unfriendly restructuring) is a real, recurring pattern that should discount conviction independent of the current catalyst's credibility

four_box.note: CDMO/CMO relationship (Rs823cr order) is a single-customer catalyst, unconfirmed as durable — tailwind weak; Rs58cr already delivered in Q1 plus existing API/diagnostics growth (+34%/+422% PAT) supports tam via the inflection rule; community itself disputes whether this is sticky CDMO vs commoditized CMO — moat no; no valuation data. 2019 SEBI ban + CBI case against promoter is a serious separate governance flag.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~55x trailing earnings on a business with ~8% ROCE and flat FY26 revenue; the multiple prices the CDMO/CMO pivot scaling into a multi-year growth + margin story -- needs ~40%+ EPS CAGR for 3-4 years to be defensible against a ~20x pharma exit
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: revenue +15-25% as the Rs 823 Cr order executes (Rs 58 Cr delivered in Q1), OPM recovering toward 10-11%, PAT sharply up off a low FY26 base
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: depends entirely on repeat CDMO orders converting the single-customer win into a pipeline; base business (API + diagnostics) grows mid-teens
market_expectation.gap_basis: a ~55x multiple already prices a durable CDMO franchise, but the order is one customer and one quarter old, the community disputes CDMO vs commoditised CMO economics, trailing ROE is negative, FCF is deeply negative on capex, and governance history (2019 SEBI ban, CBI case) warrants a discount
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

track_record.note: Per screener.in consolidated (FY16-FY26): only FY21, FY22 and FY24 cleared both >=10% revenue growth and >=15% ROCE -- FY21-22 were the COVID-diagnostics boom (ROCE 23%). FY16-20 ran ROCE 8-10%; FY25 revenue grew only 7%; FY26 revenue was flat and ROCE fell back to 8%. Not a consistent compounder.
